effect: The septum divided the heart, and the empty slots show where the two valve sets belong.

reason: The inlet valves match the heart's ventricular inlet slot.
expectation: The inlet valves should fit between the upper and lower chambers.

effect: Both valve sets are fitted, and the outlet valves limit blood flowing back from the arteries between beats.
reaction: The two valve sets' different positions and timing make their roles clearer.

reason: The pulmonary loop still has a pictured route from the heart to the lungs and back, so I'll try it with the coordinated heart.

effect: The heart is now connected to separate lung and body vessel loops.
reaction: The two routes are now visible together.

effect: The heart's own vessels had to be connected before adding blood; they supply the heart muscle separately from its chambers.
reaction: I hadn't realized the chamber blood alone couldn't feed the thick heart muscle.
reason: The connected circulation still needs blood to carry oxygen through the routes.
expectation: Blood should enter the connected circulation.

effect: Blood now fills the connected lung and body routes, completing the circulation and the chapter goals.
reaction: Seeing the full route through both sides of the heart helped put the pieces together.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the heart’s own vessels was worthwhile: it explained why the thick heart muscle needs its own blood supply, separate from blood in the chambers.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the two valve sets was clear, but matching each named valve to its slot felt fairly predictable.

surprise.text: I was surprised that blood in the heart chambers cannot by itself feed all the heart muscle.

arbitrary.text: Conducting tissue makes sense for coordinating squeezes, but needing to add it before connecting the lung route was not clear beforehand.

continue.text: I would continue: connecting the lung and body routes and discovering the heart’s own supply made me curious how the circulation supports the rest of the body.
